Commentary.Commentary: India on the other hand, bowled well. They were disciplined and also chipped away at the wickets. Shami and Bumrah impressed the most by picking 7 between them. They were well supported by the rest, especially Ishant who also kept it tight and managed to take two. Now they will have to concentrate on their batting and hope for their openers to get them off to a solid start and make the chase easier. South Africa however will look to prise out a couple of wickets by the end of today. Join us for the chase in a while.

The Proteas started off with a lead of 28 but were rocked back early by the Indians. Bumrah picked up 2 quick wickets and they were in a mush at 3 for 2. But then a 141-run stand between Elgar and de Villiers with both scoring half tons each, ensured they were back on top before the latter fell. South Africa did lose wickets at regular intervals after that but du Plessis ensured that his side gets  to a respectable total.

287 is the target for the Indians! They face an uphill task here as this is not going to be easy. They made quick work though of the remaining three wickets in this session, with Faf falling two short of his half ton. Shami, Ashwin and Bumrah all picked one wicket each in this session.

OUT! That's it! Ngidi holes out! Ashwin finally gets one, he tosses this one up on middle, Lungi tries to go over long on. He got the elevation but not the distance. Vijay in the deep runs to his right and takes an excellent catch, above his head. SOUTH AFRICA HAVE BEEN BOWLED OUT FOR 258!
That's hit the batsman high on his pads.
Tosses it up on off, Ngidi defends it onto the ground.

FOUR! WOW! Where did that come from? Bumrah lands it on a length around middle, Morkel moves his front leg out of the way and hits it over mid on for a boundary. The crowd absolutely loves it as there is a big cheer. The Indian players won't like it though.
Ngidi gets off the mark! Bumrah bowls a yorker on middle, Lungi manages to get bat on it as it rolls towards square leg for a run.
The batsman tries hooking that one but misses it completely.

Handy runs for South Africa! Bumrah bowls the third bumper of the over! Ngidi goes for the pull but it goes off the helmet and down towards third man. Kohli from first slip gives it a chase and the batsmen take two leg byes.
Another short ball on middle, Ngidi once again goes for the pull but misses. Another stifled appeal and the umpire shakes his head.
Short and down the leg side, Ngidi goes for the pull but misses and it goes to the keeper. An ambitious appeal by the Indians and the umpire shakes his head.
FOUR! Poor by Ashwin, he is gifting runs! He bowls it short on middle, Morkel rocks back and whips it through mid-wicket for a boundary. 279 is the lead can they take it up to 300?
Tosses it up on leg stump, Morkel tries to work it on the leg side but the ball bounce extra and he gets a soft leading edge towards covers.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Drags his length back, Morkel pushes it back to the bowler.
Fires it on the pads, Morkel flicks it fine down the leg side for a couple.
Shorter in length on middle, pushed to mid on.
R Ashwin is back on.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
A yorker on middle, Ngidi digs it out.
Lungi Ngidi is the last man in.

OUT! Excellent catch by Bumrah! He dropped one earlier but latches onto this one! He once again bowls another slower one on middle, Faf this time is early into the shot and it goes off the inner half to the right of the bowler who sticks his right hand out and hangs on. Jasprit is delighted as he throws the ball up in joy. He gets his third and Faf walks back after an innings which lacked intent. He falls two short of his third half ton of the series. India are one wicket away from bowling the Proteas out.
Smart bowling! Bumrah bowls the slower one. Faf reads it well too and plays it onto the ground.
Singles are on offer but Faf does not want to take them! He drives the length ball to sweeper covers but no run taken.
Back of a length on off, pushed to deep point but does not run.
Changes the angle again and bowls it from around the wicket. He bowls it on middle, Morkel plays it towards mid on.
Changes his angle but bowls it wide outside off, Morkel lets it be.
Short on the body of the batsman. Morkel ducks under it.
Lands it on a length around off, Morkel defends it.
Morne Morkel strides out.

OUT! GONE! Shami gets his fourth! He bowls it on a length around off, Rabada tries to drive it on the up with minimal feet movement. It flies off the outside edge to Kohli at second slip who does not drop this one. An early wicket for India after the break, just what they wanted. The lead is 273.
Fuller in length on off, driven towards mid off and set off for a run. The fielder scores a direct hit at the striker's end but the batsman has made it.
Another bumper on middle, this time maybe Rabada was expecting it and hence ducks under it easily.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Another bouncer, a well-directed one this time. Rabada at the very last moment evades it.
Bouncer! Down the leg side, Rabada ducks under it.
A short ball, pulled through square leg for a run.

DROPPED! That came back quickly though! Bumrah bowls it very full on middle, Faf drives it back uppishly towards the bowler who tries taking evasive action and also catch it at the same time. The ball hits him on his hands and goes onto the ground, Never looked like catching that one, Bumrah.

A low full toss on middle, Faf flicks it towards wide mid on and to everybody's surprise, Ashwin there runs to his right and stops the ball from going past him. He does not stop it cleanly but saves three.
The batsman has punched that ball through the offside.
Bowls it on a length around off, du Plessis guides it towards backward point for no run.
Good length on off, Faf defends it off the front foot.
Just behind a length on off, pushed to covers.
Length ball on off, Faf defends it.
Fuller on middle, Rabada flicks it to mid on.
Good length outside off, Rabada tries to defend but is beaten by the low bounce.
A muted appeal! Bumrah comes around the wicket and lands it on leg stump, Rabada misses the flick and the ball hits him on the pads. There is a muted appeal but the umpire shakes his head.
Better length! Bumrah has to be patient and hit those lengths consistently. He bowls it on off, du Plessis defends it.
FOUR! Up and over! Expensive start to Bumrah's over! He bangs it short on middle, Faf takes on the challenge of pulling it and he does well. He hits it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Shorter in length outside off, Faf slaps it through extra covers for a couple.
Jasprit Bumrah is back into the attack.
FOUR! Off the mark after 20 balls! A top shot to get off the mark! Shami bowls it fuller on off, Rabada times it beautifully through mid off for a boundary.
Good length on off, defended solidly.

Worked through mid-wicket with the angle and strangely Faf says no for a run. Why would he do that now? The on-air commentator mentions he does not want Rabada to face Ashwin and he would be more comfortable facing the pacers.
Good cricket all around here! Shami bowls it on a length around off, it shoots off the surface. Du Plessis does really well to hop and play that along the ground, through point for a run.
On a length around off, Faf defends it.
Fuller on middle, driven towards mid on.
Mohammed Shami will bowl from the other end. He bowled just the one over in the middle session.
Comes over the wicket and lands it on leg stump. Rabada keeps it out.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Slower through the air outside off, Rabada leaves it watchfully.
Gives it air on off, Rabada prods forward and blocks it.
Tosses it up on off, defended.
Fires it down the leg side, Rabada misses the flick.
We are back for the final session! Faf du Plessis and Kagiso Rabada will continue their innings. Ashwin will bowl the first over after the break. Here we go...
... Day 4, Session 3 ...

The lead stands at 258, and the question here is how many more do South Africa want? Will they come out with intent in the next innings or will they be happy to play out for a draw? Judging by their approach in the second session, they don't mind one. Nevertheless, the Indian side is going for it and they will look to snap up the remaining wickets quickly. A lot of questions have to be answered after the break. Join us in a while for the resumption.

A session which India will be mighty pleased with! They have not leaked runs and also managed to pick two wickets. South Africa completely lacked intent as Philander and du Plessis did not play a lot of attacking strokes and were content on defending everything that was thrown at them. They stitched a frustrating stand of 46 of 156 balls which was eventually broken by Ishant Sharma. He picked both the wickets to fall in this session and has been the pick of the bowlers for the away side.
FOUR! 3000 runs for Faf du Plessis in Tests and he gets there in style! Short and on the body, Faf swivels and pulls it through backward square leg for a boundary.

Ohkay! A friendly warning there by Kohli to Rabada as he left the non-striker's crease even before the ball was dead. Kohli could have inflicted a run out but instead complained to the umpire about it and the umpire too had a word with Rabada about the same. Don't think he will be leaving the crease now.
Bowls it on middle, worked to mid-wicket.
Good bowling! Very full and tailing back in late. Faf drives it back towards Shami.
Good length on off, stays a touch low. Du Plessis gets it off the bottom towards mid on.
Slower ball on a fuller length on off, the batsman mistimes it to mid on.
Bowls it on a length outside off, Faf lets it be.
Mohammed Shami is back into the attack.
Length on middle, Rabada defends it.
Just short! A length ball on middle, Rabada flicks it uppishly but short of short mid-wicket.
Shorter in length on the body of the batsman, cramping him for room. Rabada tucks it to square leg.
Back of a length on off, taps it towards cover-point for a run.
Angles it on the pads, worked to mid-wicket.
Good length on off, Faf defends it off the front foot.
The second new ball is now due! Will India take it? No they don't and Pandya continues.
Defends the ball on off, of the front foot.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
BEATEN! Ashiwn gives it air and bowls it on off, it turns away and also bounces. Rabada tries to defend by lunging forward but is beaten.
The straighter one outside off, Kagiso lets it be.
Tosses it up on off, it turns away sharply. Rabada goes for the booming drive but misses. The ball beats the keeper and even goes past the diving slip fielder for two byes.
Fires it on middle, Rabada defends it.
Change of ends for Ashwin! More than ends I think he has been brought in for the left-hander who is on strike.
FOUR! This is Faf's first boundary in this session! Pandya bowls it on a length outside off, offers a little width. Du Plessis times it through covers for a boundary. The lead is now 250.
Another ball on a length around off, du Plessis defends it by taking his hand off the handle.
Fullish ball on middle, swings in late. FDP flicks it to mid on.
On a length around off, defended towards mid-wicket.
Works it around the corner with the angle.
Right on the money first up! He lands it on a length around off, Faf defends it off the front foot.
Just one over for Ashwin! Hardik Pandya is back into the attack.
Shortish ball on middle, Rabada ducks under it.
Nicely bowled! Making good use of the angle, Ishant. He has his tail up here. He comes running in and lands it on a length around off, it angles away. Rabada tries to defend but is beaten.
Short and wide outside off, not a lot of fizz off the surface. Rabada watches it go through to the keeper.
Slower ball outside off, Faf reads it early and strokes it through covers for a run.
Fuller in length on off, FDP crisply times it to covers.
Good length on off, stays a touch low. Faf tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
A single to end the over! Faf pushes it through covers for a run.

Flighted ball outside off, it turns back in sharply. Faf tries to defend but coming out of the line of off but misses. It hits him on top of the pad and lobs towards Sharma at first slip. There is an appeal for LBW first and then for a catch but the umpire stays put.
The batsman has played it fine down the leg side.
Floats it up on middle, Faf tries to work it but it goes off the glove to leg slip.
Flatter on off, Faf gets an outside edge through short third man for a couple.
Tosses it up on off, Faf defends it.
Kagiso Rabada walks in at no. 9. Meanwhile, R Ashwin is back into the attack.

OUT! Another one bites the dust! Ishant Sharma roars in celebration as he gets his second in consecutive overs. He bowls it on a length around off, it straightens a touch and also gets big on the batsman. Maharaj pokes at it and gets an outside edge to the keeper, Patel, who takes it. Maharaj walks back early and the Indians are back in the game now.
The ball is down the leg side but the batsman still goes after it.
A bumper on middle, Maharaj ducks under it.

FOUR! Off the bottom! Ishant serves a full toss down the leg side. All Maharaj has to do is put bat on it. He does so but does not get it off the middle, it goes off the bottom and down to fine leg for a boundary.
Fullish ball outside off, Maharaj lets it be.
Good length on off, Maharaj defends it towards covers.
Shorter in length outside off, this one stays low. Faf is beaten by the low bounce as he tries to cut. End of a maiden over by Pandya.
Sprays it down the leg side, FDP lets it be.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
On the pads, Faf tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.

EDGED AND GONE! No wait... the umpire does not think so! Hardik though was adamant there was an edge there. He bowls it short and outside off, Faf goes for the square cut but seems to have missed it. Parthiv dives to his right and collects the ball. Hardik makes a huge appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Pandya wants it to be reviewed but neither  does the keeper nor his captain agree and hence they don't. Hardik walks back to his mark in anger but Parthiv for once was right there as replays later on show there was no edge.
Good length on off, du Plessis defends it solidly.
Errs in line and bowls it down the leg side. Maharaj misses the flick and the umpire signals a wide.
Another good delivery on middle, swinging back in. Maharaj tries to defend but it takes the inside edge through square leg for a couple.
Keshav Maharaj walks out to the middle. Also in the meantime the ball has been changed for mystery reasons.

OUT! ISHANT STRIKES! The frustrating 46-run stand off 156 balls  has been broken! Sharma gets his first and he is ecstatic. He bangs it short on middle, Philander plays the pull shot but does not time it. It lobs towards Murali Vijay, who is standing in front of square, for an easy catch. Philander walks back after playing a gritty knock. Also, the nature of this partnership has not let the game slip away from India, this wicket has now brought the visitors back in it. Can they now trigger a collapse? The lead is 3 short of 240.
Just ahead of a length on off, worked to mid-wicket. Ishant tumbles onto the ground on his followthrough but he is back up again.
That has come in appreciably! Ishant bowls it on a length around off, it shapes in late. Philander chops it to gully.
Length on middle, Philander defends it towards mid on.
Sprays it on the pads, Philander works it through mid-wicket to move to his 26th run.
Another ball on a length around off, Philander works it towards mid-wicket.
An off cutter on middle, Philander blocks it.
India trying everything to take a wicket here as Pandya comes around the wicket and angles it across the batsman. Vernon defends it towards the cover region and thinks for a run but is sent back.
Finally a shot with intent but does not time it! Pandya bowls it a touch shorter on middle, Philander tries to pull but mistimes it to mid-wicket.
Pandya has been consistently bowling on a length. He does the same here on off, Philander defends it.
Bowls it on a length on off, du Plessis plants his front foot forward and defends it.
Another length ball outside off, Faf lets it be.
Arieal but well short! India are desperate for a wicket and they need this to go to hand. Ishant bowls a inswinger on middle, Faf flicks it uppishly but well short of Kohli.
Another ball pitched on a length, in the zone outside off. FDP shoulders arms to it.
Another ball pitched on a length, in the zone outside off. FDP shoulders arms to it.
Ishant has managed to keep it tight! He bowls it on a length around off, Faf defends it solidly.
Angles it on the pads, Philander works it towards short mid-wicket.
Good length ball on off, Pandya defends it solidly.
Length ball outside off, Plessis guides it down to third man for a run.

There is a leg gully and Pandya is bowling to his field but Philander is playing it well. Hardik bowls it a touch shorter, aims it at the rib cage of the batsman. Vernon, quite comfortably tucks it around the corner for a run.
Angling into the batsman, he hops and flicks it to mid-wicket.
Attacks the stumps on a length. Philander defends it back towards the bowler.

The drinks break comes as a respite from this monotonous bat-ball contest (actually a no contest at the moment). At the moment it just seems as if players from one side are running in with a red round object in their hands and landing it in an area for the wooden object to make contact. Du Plessis has found a wonderful confidant in Philander who has helped him string a 43-run stand off 133 balls. 10 overs to go for the second new ball and that would be the only thing that we can look forward to unless there's something in the drinks that spurs the Indians up. Let's see what's in store for the remaining part of this session. The lead at this point is 66 less than 300.
Another ball around off, kept out from the crease towards the cover region for nothing.
This length delivery is played off the back foot defensively towards covers.
Bowled on the pads, Vernon fails to flick it and gets it through backward square leg off his pads. A leg bye signaled as a run is taken.
Philander stands tall and presents a dead bat to keep it out.
Very full on off, dug out to covers. Shouts of encouragement still heard. Wonder where the energy comes for them to go on egging even when nothing is happening.
Length ball on off, kept out with a straight bat towards the bowler.
This is fuller outside off, driven to mid off.
Full on off, driven back to the bowler.
No short leg this time and Philander uses that spot to take his 24th run. He flicks it aerially through that spot and gets to the other end. He overtakes du Plessis now.
Philander blocks it off the back foot.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
This is full outside off, driven to covers.
Fuller and straighter on the stumps, pushed back to the bowler.
Easy this. Length delivery on the pads, nudged down to fine leg for one. The stand is worth 41 runs now off 121 balls. Shows the time it had taken to come.

Bouncer around off, pulled all along the ground to deep square leg for one. Often we don't appreciate the beauty of this stroke as the replay makes me do. Faf had his eyes on the ball till the end and roll his hand on that to ensure he doesn't hit it aerially.

Well bowled. Hurled just outside off, du Plessis looks to play it through the off side. Gets undone by the low bounce and gets beaten on the inside. The ball goes on the bounce to Patel. Shows the slow pace of the track.
Fuller outside off, left alone.
Short and angling down leg, Faf leaves it alone.

Communicating in a language which is not known to the opposition is so useful.... when India were batting we observed that Virat Kohli was talking in Hindi with his partners. Now, Faf du Plessis follows that principle and is talking to Vernon Philander in Afrikaans. Could have translated what he said... only if we knew that language... anyone willing to help?
Hardik comes round the wicket and bowls it on the pads. The Protea skipper works it away to fine leg for one. The lead moves to 230 now.
This one is played off the front foot towards mid on.
Shorter in length, Philander looks to pull it. Ends up getting an inside edge onto his pads and the ball rolls through backward square leg for one.
This is well outside off, left alone. The pace reads as 141 kph.

Off cutter outside off, Philander goes for the drive through covers. Seems to have inside edged it. The ball goes on the bounce to Patel, who fails to gather it. Replays show the absence of an edge there as the ball spun in from the surface with a puff of dust.
Fuller and angling in, worked with the line to short mid-wicket.
On the pads, worked away to the on side. A good maiden over from the lanky pacer.
Du Plessis stands tall and blocks it down.
The batsman failed to make contact and was hit low on the pads.
This ball is defended awkwardly towards point.

Gone! Oh no! KI, my colleague's reaction made me type so excitedly. It is bowled on a length just outside off, this one unlike others doesn't move away. It holds its line even as Faf is forced to defend it away from his body. Seems like a tickling sound came as the ball passed the willow but no other Indian on the field there felt so.
Kept out off the back foot to the off side.

Quick run there. Faf punches this towards covers and takes off to the other end quickly. There is a shy at the batter's end but it doesn't hit the stumps there even as Philander strives to make it in and does eventually. Patel dives to back the throw up. The 200th South African run is up here, the overall lead 28 more than that figure.
Length ball on off, defended off the back foot.
Fuller outside off, driven powerfully to covers.

The decision wasn't surprising as it turns out. NOT OUT! Looked so to the naked eye as well, but it turns out closer than we thought. Pandya hurls this on a length around off and coming in. Du Plessis seems to be taken aback by something as he indicated so after missing the flick and getting hit on the front pad. Pandya says that there's no inside edge and hence Kohli, after asking someone else as well, perhaps the keeper, opts for the DRS. Time for a re-look. No inside edge on that as seen from the Snicko. Hawk Eye says that it would go on to clip the top of the leg stumps but the smallest of margins. Hence it is umpire's call and the on-field call stays. Thankfully for India and Kohli, the review is retained.
Another review taken, more in hope than conviction. It is for LBW against du Plessis again. Seems to be sliding down leg...
Length ball angling in, du Plessis lets it come to him and directs it to short leg.
Philander nudges this towards fine leg. Patel runs to it and gets it. One run taken.
Similar ball, defended towards point where Vijay fields. Two runs off this over, SA two short of reaching 200.
Length ball in a line just outside off. Vernon opens the face of the bat to guide it to the man at deep backward point for a single.
A bit of shape this time. Fuller in length, moves away a touch. Squares du Plessis a bit and he ends up getting an outside edge through backward point for one.
Drags his length back this time, defended with a straight bat towards covers.
Fuller outside off, driven to the man stationed at covers.
Hurled on a length on off, Faf keeps it out with a block from the crease.
Ishant Sharma to roll his arm from the other end now. He's wicketless in this innings so far. The hosts at this stage are ahead by 224.
Off cutter outside off, Vernon covers his stumps to let it go. It goes on the bounce to the keeper.
Much better delivery from Pandya. Gets it to jag back in from a length around off. Philander gets his bat down in a hurry and ends up getting it off the inner half on his front pad.
The on-air commentators inform us that this session and the next one is extended by 15 minutes to make up for the time lost yesterday.
Length ball on off, blocked from the crease.
Short leg in place now.
Patted towards covers for one.
Bowled down the leg side, Faf misses his flick.
On a length around off, defended from the crease.
Hardik Pandya to bowl for the first time in this innings.
FOUR! Strays on the pads and pays the price. Bumrah bowls this full in length, Philander just helps it across to the fine leg fence.
This ball is defended from the front foot onto the ground.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Faf looks to work this to the on side but ends up getting a leading edge towards covers.
Length ball on off defended from the crease.

NOT OUT! Bat only! Weirdest of reviews from India. Bumrah runs in and slips in a yorker in line of the stumps. Du Plessis seems to have dug it out well but his front leg was also close to the bat. India appeal but fail to get the desired decision. Kohli asks Parthiv, Pujara at covers and then the bowler before signaling for the DRS. The first replay itself embarrasses the Indians as there doesn't seem to be anything on that except the bat. Wonder why the bowler didn't spot this and help the skipper out in making a wise use of the review. One less for India now.
Bat first? Toe first? India appeal for an LBW against du Plessis. On not getting the nod, they go upstairs after conferring amongst themselves.
Patted towards covers for one to retain strike.
Floated around middle, du Plessis comes down the track to work it away to the on side. Kohli does well now to stop it with a dive and prevent a run.
Worked towards mid on for one.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
This is flicked to square leg off the back foot.
Nicely done, Puji! Tossed up ball around off, worked away towards mid-wicket. Pujara from square leg runs to his left and keeps it down to one with a dive.
This is defended off the front foot solidly.
Fuller on off, played to covers.

Good work but not so good! Driven on the up towards mid off. Ishant gets to his left, does well to put in the slide. But ends up parrying it back without stopping it cleanly. Ends up conceding a brace. He nails down the stumps at the bowler's end with the throw due to which Bumrah appeals. Michael Holding gives reply to that on air, saying du Plessis wouldn't be too careless to do what Pandya did. Sums it up.
Length ball angling in, Philander misses the flick and wears it high on the pads. An appeal follows but doesn't get the desired nod.
This one is blocked towards covers for nothing.
Straighter in line of the stumps, flicked to mid-wicket.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
Now a run taken after VP turns this away past short leg.
Flatter on the pads, turned away to the on side.
Floated full on off, driven back down the ground powerfully. Ashwin does well to make a half-stop there, nothing conceded though.
Bunted off the front foot onto the ground.

FOUR! Too full that, grunts Michael Holding on air. Playing against the turn isn't easy and Philander needs to be credited for that here. Floated full and outside off, Philander gets his front foot down and drives it nicely through covers. Gets a boundary as a result.
Flicked away off the pads for one to retain strike.

Yorker! Well played in the end, you've to say. My colleague Rish was just ranting as to why a good limited overs bowler like Bumrah isn't bowling a yorker to a lower order bat like Vernon. He gets his wish fulfilled here. But Vernon negotiates it well. Looks to dig it out but gets hit low on the pads. Question asked from the bowler, no response from the ump.
Fuller on the stumps, stonewalled from the crease.
Length ball angling in at the stumps, Philander presents a straight bat to block it back towards the bowler. More shouts to cheer up the bowler from Kohli.
Bumper on the stumps, Vernon ducks.
This is bowled outside off, pushed towards point. Shouts of encouragement heard from the Indian skipper.
Nicely played. Vernon pushes this through covers for one to retain strike.
Ashwin comes over the wicket now. Serves it just outside off, defended off the front foot onto the ground.
Faf uses his feet to get to the pitch of the ball and works it through mid-wicket for one.
Philander lets this come to the bat and pats it towards covers for one.
Similar ball, worked away wide of mid on for a run.
Starts round the wicket and bowls it around middle. Faf prods forward in defense.
As expected, Ravichandran Ashwin to bowl from the other end. Strangely, he hasn't got much off the surface today, the rain affecting the surface perhaps.
Fuller in length, Philander comes forward in defense.

Sunil Gavaskar on air says that there are cracks on the surface but they are more horizontal. These won't affect the batters as much as the vertical ones would, he opines. Explains why there hasn't been much to look forward to for the bowlers.
This ball is flicked to the man at mid-wicket for nothing.
Vernon stays put on the back foot in defending this from the crease.
Loud call in affirmation for a run from du Plessis after driving it towards wide mid off. Ishant does the mop up but a single taken easily.
This is well outside off, played through the point region for a single. Philander moves to 4, lead to 202.
Fuller ball on off to start off, defended off the front foot towards covers.

We're back! Good to have you with us. The South African lead stands at 201 at this point, with half the side still in the hut. Out come the players and the umpires as well. This session will begin with Vernon Philander facing Jasprit Bumrah first up. Faf du Plessis waits at the other end. Kohli has tended to have this fielder often in this game - the widish first slip. Has him again. Here we go...
... Penultimate Day, Penultimate Session ...

Ashwin toiled around unsuccessfully for 22 overs. Shami was the man who ran in and troubled the hosts with the ball. The scalps that he got were a just reward for his efforts. What can we expect next? Perhaps more screams from Kohli. More plays and misses, maybe. Some more attritional cricket definitely. See you soon on the other side.

Elgar and de Villiers looked assured when they started off. They stitched together a 141-run stand, the highest in this series so far. Although the former looked a touch fidgety, the latter more-than-compensated for that and was unlucky to fall short of his century by 20 runs. That gave India the little opening they needed and they picked up a couple more soon after. More fortunate were they to prise out Elgar as well.

26 overs, 83 runs, 3 wickets - these are the relevant figures for this session. The over rate is 13. Not encouraging. India should have slipped in a few more overs in a bid to eke out some more wickets but that's not to be. Aakash Chopra had tweeted this morning that India shouldn't expect a session filled with wickets and should be happy with something around 75/4 this morning. That's what has happened so far.
Floated outside off, defended off the front foot towards short leg. LUNCH on the penultimate day!
Ash comes round the wicket and lands it around middle and leg, turned towards mid-wicket.
Du Plessis presses forward and bunts it down.
This one is clipped towards mid-wicket.
Good umpiring. Philander was trying some time-wasting tactics there to which the umpire says that 'you can do it after Lunch'.
Similar line, Faf offers no stroke and wears it on the pads.
Flatter outside off, Faf goes across and pads it out.
Around off, blocked off the back foot.
This ball is kept out towards mid off.
Loud clear call for YES from the Protea skipper as soon as he hit it towards wide mid off. A run completed with ease.
Fuller on off, driven towards mid off.
This one is punched off the back foot towards covers.
Around off, du Plessis mistimes his punch back towards the bowler.
Jasprit Bumrah back on.
Vernon has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Ashwin comes round the wicket and lands it around leg. Philander goes back to flick but it goes off his thigh pad to Rahul at short leg. All the close in fielders apart from him go up in appeal. He knew it perhaps.
Again placed to the same area.
Tossed up on off, defended towards mid-wicket off the front foot.
Flatter on the pads, kept down to leg slip.
This ball is punched off the back foot.
Knocked him over? No! It seemed so at the first look that Shami had breached du Plessis defense. But it struck his thigh pad and rolled to the slip cordon. Lovely ball to end the over.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Run, run, run, shouts du Plessis as he flicks it through square leg. Pandya dives in the deep and keeps them down to two. The lead now reached double ton.

Confusion again, could have proved fatal for sure. Philander works it towards square leg and sets off for a run. This time Faf responds. Kohli from mid-wicket gets there and fires a wild throw at the striker's end. Du Plessis would have been a goner had he hit.
This is defended to the on side.

Early loud call from Faf! Remember the Philander-du Plessis history, right? In the first essay, there was a terrible mix up that resulted in the former's wicket. Here the skipper doesn't want that to happen. Vernon taps this towards covers and sets off for a run. A loud call from the opposite end makes him abort the idea.
In line of the stumps, back foot defense on display.
Flatter on the pads, flicked away towards short leg.
Vernon works it through mid-wicket for one.

Spiteful turn at Centurion! Yes, you read that right. Tossed up outside off, the ball takes a puff of dust from the surface and spins in sharply. Philander has to go back hurriedly to keep it out and ends up almost playing it on from between his legs.
Played through mid-wicket by VP.
Floated around off, full in length, swept away to deep square leg for one.
Du Plessis is not ready. He has some issues with the sightscreen and tells Ashwin to stop in his run up.
Fuller on off, defended towards mid on.
Banged in line of the stumps, ducked under by Vernon.
Full and slanting in, clipped away to fine leg for one. Pandya does the mopping up there. He hasn't worn that white lip guard today and hence my partner here failed to recognise him.
Another one outside off, left alone.
This is bowled outside off, shouldered arms to by FDP.
Stifled appeal, all good. Full and angling down leg, Faf misses the flick to get hit on the pads. Low toned appeal to no avail.
Vernon defends it from within the crease.
Blocked towards mid-wicket from the crease.
Floated on the stumps, swept away for one.
Kept out from the back foot.
Eased through mid on for a run to get off the mark.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
That ball has struck the batsman on the thigh-pad. The batsmen have run through for a single. The Umpire signals Leg Bye.
This is outside off, left alone.
The next man in for South Africa is Vernon Philander. My colleague observes that whenever he laughs, a wicket goes down off the next one and that's what has happened even here.

OUT! De Kock was trying hard to get out and he does edge one eventually! Generally bowlers strive hard to take a wicket but here it is the southpaw who tried hard and succeeded in gifting one here. Edged the previous three balls and got boundaries (the last one seemed an edge at the first glance). This one is edged again but goes straight into Parthiv's gloves. No mistake this time by the Indian keeper. Hard to understand why you'd play at that repeatedly. Credit to Shami to be bowling in that channel of uncertainty. India making steady inroads now.

FOUR! Streaky yet again! This time there is a second slip in place, Rohit Sharma. De Kock plays at this length ball away from his body yet again. Perhaps opens the face of his bat at the last moment and gets it well past Sharma for a boundary.

FOUR! Another edge, another boundary. Length ball just outside off, de Kock hangs his bat out that. Gets a thick outside edge that flies past the keeper and to the fence. This time Patel dives to his left but fails to reach that.
FOUR! Slash and slash hard! That's what de Kock has done to get off the pair here. Length ball outside off, he goes hard at it and edges it just over the leaping Kohli at wide slip to get a boundary.
Another one on the pads, worked round the corner.
FDP has flicked the ball off his pads.
On the pads, flicked away.
This is defended off the front foot onto the ground.

Dropped! Tough one though. These are the ones that stick, actually. Served on the pads, du Plessis looks to work it away with the angle. Gets finer than he would have liked. Rahul at backward short leg dives full length to his right but fails to hang on this time. How costly will this be. Full marks for the attempt though.
This one is flicked away towards mid-wicket.
Length ball around off, kept out from the crease.
Quinton de Kock walks in next. One southpaw replaces the other and this is now a good time for him to get some runs under his belt. He is on a pair, remember.

OUT! Is this the big moment that India need? The change of angle works for Shami. He comes round the wicket and bangs it short just outside off. It is angled in as well. Elgar instinctively goes for the hook and fails to account for the fielder placed  in the deep. Hits it straight down Rahul's throat at deep backward square leg. He fumbles on the first attempt but manages to cling on and looks relieved to have done that. Another set batter departs and Elgar, who was largely unconvincing in his stay out there walks back 39 short of his ton. They are now 179/4 effectively.
In line of the stumps, defended off the front foot.
Full and straight down the leg side, DE misses the flick.
This is bowled outside off, pushed towards point.
Square leg goes back. Shall we expect a bouncer?
Length ball angling in, nudged down to fine leg for one.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

The occasional ball turns like this and beats the batter all ends up. Ashwin tosses it generously around off, Elgar goes back to play it but gets beaten by the away spin. Parthiv's glovework has been shoddy and here again he fails to collect that.
Dean has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
On the pads flicked away towards mid-wicket.
Tossed up outside off, defended towards covers.
The short of length delivery has been cut away through square on the off side.
This delivery is kept out off the back foot. A maiden from Shami now.
Length ball outside off, punched towards covers. Pujara does well there with a dive.
Full in line of the stumps, driven back down the ground. Mid on gets to his left and intercepts it.
Almost gone. Shami hurls it on a length outside off, Faf has a feel for that and just gets beaten. Wasn't far from kissing the outside edge of the blade.
Angling in to the batter from over the wicket, flicked straight to the man at mid-wicket.
Fuller on off and middle, Faf stays in the crease and defends it out.
Elgar stays on the back foot and presents a straight bat in negotiating this one.
Played to the point region by DE.
This one is flicked away round the corner for one. Brings up 150 for South Africa and now they are ahead by 178.

FOUR! Nice way to get off the mark. Du Plessis does not seem to be out there to block his way out. Sees this flighted ball outside off, Faf gets outside off and plays the sweep. Gets it off the bottom of his bat but that's enough to help the ball roll to the fine leg fence for a boundary.
Flatter on off, defended from the crease.
Floated outside off, Elgar gets it off the outer half past silly point for one.
Length ball on off, FDP defends it solidly.
The batsman has driven it through mid on.
Good length outside off, the batsman lets it be.
On a length around off, Faf lets it be.
Another length delivery outside around off, Faf defends it solidly.
Faf du Plessis is the next man in.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Shami gets the big fish! A huge wicket for India, the breakthrough they needed. He lands it on a length around off, gets some extra bounce off the surface with some movement inwards. De Villiers tries to guide it down to third man but is surprised by the extra bounce. He tries to pull his bat out of the way but is too late in doing that. The ball takes the edge and goes to Parthiv who makes no mistake. The 141-run stand comes to an end and India will now look to capitalize. The lead is now 172.
BEATEN! How many times did we see this yesterday? Ashwin tosses it up on off, turns away sharply. Elgar tries to defend it off the back foot but is beaten again.
Edge but short! Ashwin tosses this one up on off, it turns away. Elgar tries to defend but it goes off the edge but well short of Kohli.
Works it with the spin through mid-wicket for a run.
Driven towards the mid on region. They pick up a single.
De Villiers brings out the reverse sweep this time and he connects well. India do have a fielder for that shot in the deep and only a single results.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Angles it into the batsman, defended towards mid on. 9 runs from the over, an expensive first by Shami.
Back of a length on off, defended towards point.
FOUR! Second boundary of the over! Not a good start by Shami. He comes around the wicket and angles it in on shorter length. Too easy for Elgar as he pulls it through square leg for a boundary.
Works the length ball around the corner for a run.
This was nicely played by AB! Shami bowls it fuller on off, it tails back in late. De Villiers drives it to mid on.

FOUR! Welcome to the bowling crease Shami! You just can't offer width to this guy he will pounce on it. Shami bowls it short outside off, a loosener. De Villiers guides it through backward point and into the fence.
Mohammed Shami is into the attack now.
Floated on off, defended stoutly.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR! Not in convincing fashion but Elgar won't mind! Ashwin tosses it up on middle, Elgar moves his front leg out of the way, he takes the aerial route but does not connect it well. It still has enough to clear mid on. It lands just inside the boundary rope and trickles away.
The batsman has played it to the point region.
There is no pace at all on this wicket. Ashwin bowls it on middle, it comes quite slow off the surface. Elgar rocks back and works it to mid-wicket.
Another tossed up ball on middle, Elgar defends it.
Once again bowls it on a length around off, Elgar defends it towards point for a quick run. 5 runs from the over.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Bowls it on a length outside off, Elgar lets it be.

FOUR! Fifty for Elgar and he gets there with the most convincing shot he has played till now. It is his 9th in this format. He gets a half-volley outside off, Elgar leans into it and drives it through extra covers for a boundary.
Good lengths hit by Ishant! He bowls it on off, Elgar defends it onto the ground.
Another good ball outside off, Elgar lets it be. He also dishes out some words to Elgar.
FOUR! Excellent shot! De Villiers goes down on one knee, he sweeps the ball with the spin and into the square leg fence. 151 is the lead now.
Tosses it up on off, de Villiers defends it off the front foot.
Another short ball outside off, the ball comes very slow off the surface. De Villiers has all the time in the world to rock back and punch it through covers for a couple.
Gives it air on off, de Villiers lunges forward and defends it.
Shorter in length on middle, Elgar works it against the spin, through mid-wicket for a run.
He starts off with a tossed up delivery outside off, Elgar waits for the ball to do its bit and defends it.
R Ashwin is into the attack.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Another appeal but the keeper is not at all interested! Ishant bowls it down the leg side, AB goes for the flick but it goes off something to the keeper. The bowler and some of the fielders make a huge shout but there is nothing from the keeper. Replays later on show that it had flicked the thigh pad.
Works it to mid-wicket with the angle.
FOUR! Excellent placement! Ishant bowls it short and outside off, de Villiers places it through point for a boundary.
Oooo! That almost kisses the outside edge. Ishant bowls it in the zone outside off, it moves away after pitching and de Villiers is beaten as he tries to play for the natural angle.
Just behind a length on off, de Villiers defends it.
Good length on middle, Elgar defends it back to the bowler.
On the pads, Elgar flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple.

BEATEN! Excellent delivery! Elgar has looked so unconvincing out there but he is surviving! Bumrah comes running in and angles it into the batsman, it straightens after pitching around off. Elgar tries to defend but is beaten.

EDGY FOUR! Kohli should have stopped that! Bumrah lands it on a length around off, it straightens a touch, Elgar tries to defend but it goes off the outside edge but well short of Kohli at widish first slip who puts in a half-hearted effort and lets it through for a boundary.

Another length ball outside off, de Villiers taps it towards gully and he sets off for a run. He is sent back by his partner as there wasn't one. The fielder there has a shy but misses and the batsmen eventually run one on the overthrow.
Lands it on a length around off, de Villiers tries to tap it for a run but it goes straight to the fielder and it is a dot ball.
Another ball outside off, guided towards point for a run.
On a length around off, there is no movement on offer. De Villiers shuffles and defends it onto the ground.
Bowls it down the leg side, de Villiers tries to flick but misses.
Worked to mid-wicket for no runs.

Excellent running! De Villiers is very quick between the wickets. He guides the ball outside off, towards deep backward point for a couple. The 100-run stand is also up between the two. This is the first of this match and it is also taking the game away from the Indians.
Lands it on a length outside off, the batsman lets it be.
Just behind a length outside off, de Villiers cuts it through point for a run.

That has not bounced at all! Lucky for de Villiers it was not on the stumps. Bumrah bowls it on a length outside off, it stays very low. De Villiers is beaten as he tries to defend and the ball goes under his bat and along the ground to Patel who for once does well behind the stumps.
Fullish ball on middle, de Villiers mistimes it to mid on.
Fuller in length on off, driven to mid off.
Another single, the Indians need to stop South Africa from taking these singles. Elgar drops it towards point for a quick run.
Shortish outside off, offers a little width. Enough for de Villiers to cut it through point. There is a fielder in the deep so only a single results. Also the 100 is up for the hosts.
On a length outside off, Elgar makes a leave.
Well bowled! Ishant bowls it on a length around off, Elgar lunges forward and defends it.
Angles it on the pads, de Villiers flicks it down to fine leg to change strike.
On a length around off, defended towards point.

A big appeal! Ishant was pleading there. Sharma comes running in and angles it into the batsman. AB de Villiers tries to flick but misses it to get hit on the pads. Ishant makes a loud appeal, an extended one but the umpire shakes his head. The Indians think about a review but then opt against it. Good they did not as replays later on show it was sliding down leg.
Length ball outside off, Elgar taps it towards covers for a run.
Good length on off, de Villiers defends it stoutly.
Another ball on the shorter side for outside off, Elgar punches it through point for a run. Partnership between the two is 94 now and the lead is 125.
A single to follow up! On a length on off, de Villiers works it towards wide mid on for a run. He is such a busy player, always looking to score.
FOUR! Classic shot! Bumrah bowls it slightly fuller on off, AB leans into it and drives it on the up and through covers for the first boundary of the day.
Flicks it with the angle towards mid-wicket.
Comes running in and bowls it from wide of the crease. Bumrah lands it on a length around off, defended towards mid off.
Jasprit Bumrah will bowl from the other end.
Comes around the wicket to the left-hander and lands it on a length around off. Elgar defends it solidly.
Better line! He bowls it around off, on a length. The batsman tries to defend but it goes off the inner half towards square leg for the first run for the day.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Another leave to a delivery outside off.
So Ishant Sharma starts off with two balls outside off, harmless deliveries. De Villiers need not play at those.
Starts off with a loosener outside off, de Villiers watchfully makes a leave.

We are all set for the action to begin. A new day and we hope to see a less agitated Kohli. He and his teammates make their way out to the middle. For South Africa, AB de Villiers and Dean Elgar will continue their innings. A minimum of 98 overs will be bowled today as we lost overs yesterday, due to rain and then bad light. Ishant Sharma will be bowling the first today. He has a widish slip in place. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT -  Shaun Pollock and Kepler Wessels say the pitch looks the same and the cracks have also not opened up. Admit there is some variable bounce as seen yesterday in the two dismissals. Inform there is a little bit for the spinners and it will be difficult for the left-handers while facing Ashwin. State there is not a lot of rough outside the right-handers off stump. End by saying it is about getting through the first twenty minutes and then it will ease out a little.

For the visitors, wickets is what they need and that too in heaps. A lot will depend on Ashwin, who has got good purchase out of the surface. We might see him do the bulk of the bowling today, like he has done in this game. The Indians would fancy their chances chasing anything under 250 on a wicket which does not have a lot of demons. The first session is a very important and we welcome you for our coverage. Stay tuned...

We head into day 4 of the second Test between South Africa and India in Centurion with the game evenly poised or slightly in the favor of the hosts, you can say. They lead by 118 and one good session for them can see the game tilt towards them completely. They still have 8 wickets in hand and they would now look to stretch the lead to as much as possible. Remember they have their savior, AB de Villiers, at the crease who is unbeaten on a half ton.
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

South Africa will aim to put a tall score on board and aided with the lead of the first innings, they'll look to put this game beyond India. But this is easier said than done. The visiting team is intent on not letting the game and the series slip and hence will leave no stone unturned in battling it out. It'll want to run through the Protea batting and have a shot at maintaining Kohli's clean slate as far his captaincy record is concerned. Do join us to find out exactly how the day draws out. See you at 1000 local time (0800 GMT) then. Till then, bubye! Take care.

Earlier in the day, the tourists were wrapped up soon after Lunch. Their innings had one big score from Kohli, who was the last man dismissed on 153. A useful 71-run partnership with Ashwin helped India reduce the margin of deficit in the first innings. For the Proteas, Morkel stood out with a four-fer while the others chipped in with one wicket apiece.

After Tea, we had only 10 overs possible, that too in a couple of installments. Even in that passage, a chance went down. This innings of Elgar will be remembered for him coming out with his dancing shoes on and not the sports one. That phase would have culminated with his dismissal but Patel was too generous or, lazy shall we say, as he didn't go for it. The southpaw has done well to string an unbeaten 87-run stand with de Villiers, who walked in when his side was in a mush. The former skipper has done well to help them out of it, going past 50 for the 42nd time in this format. Both of them have helped the lead swell to 118.

So, there we go! The news that became more obvious as time passed by, arrives. PLAY CALLED OFF FOR THE  DAY! Rain first and bad light later, rob us of an exciting end to the day. This scenario can well be likened to a good thrilling movie whose poor climax spoils all the fun of watching it. The game is tantalizingly poised at this stage. Like the first Test, we do not seem to have an early start tomorrow. The extra 8 overs would be squeezed in the three sessions each, of the remaining two days.

1710 local time update - It is now past the usual scheduled time for Stumps. Hard to see play resuming past this point, given how dark it was when players walked off. Perhaps the officials won't risk resumption given the mood Kohli was in. The updates from the venue state that covers are drawn even though there is no rain there.

Meanwhile, Virat Kohli and Ravi Shastri are seen having a word with the match referee and the former seems extremely agitated. Not sure what exactly is the issue, but there are rules in place, there are umpires to monitor the game, so he needn't be so animated. Contrastingly, Faf du Plessis and his boys are seen sitting calmly in their dressing room, keeping an eye on whatever is going on in the match referee's cabin. Nevertheless, that's what we have for the time being. Stay tuned for further updates.

Bad news, folks, again! Not rain, but BAD LIGHT forces the players out this time. The on-field umpires are seen taking the reading on the light meters. This is the benchmark set for the game, meaning, the same level of visibility will result in the game halting for the remaining duration of it.
Another one full on off, blocked from the front foot onto the ground.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Gets the one run, finally, that takes him to his 42nd TEST FIFTY. Gets a fuller ball on off, de Villiers taps it towards covers and hares across to the other end. There was a shy at the keeper's end but Elgar was well in even as the ball missed the stumps there.
Another one, beaten all ends up. Hurled on a length outside off, closer to the off stick. De Villiers has to play for it but gets beaten by a small margin. This sport is about inches, mind you.

Lovely, lovely ball. On a length just outside off, de Villiers has to play at that. Hangs his bat out but the ball misses the outside edge by just. Patel catches that and puts in an appeal, a shake of head from Bumrah himself.
Length ball outside off, AB dabs it through point and helps himself to a brace. Moves to 49 with that. The lead is 117 now.
Elgar picked that bouncer early and let it through to the keeper.

Interesting. Kohli and Rohit are standing at first and second slips respectively now. Well, on that previous occasion, Pujara wasn't at fault and he was proving to be a safe hand at first slip in the recent games.
Angling in from round the wicket, bowled on a length around off and middle. Elgar plays it towards mid-wicket.
Sprayed down the leg side, Dean lets it be.
Fuller outside off, de Villiers slices this to third man for one.
The batsman fails to put bat on ball.
Shami bowls this on a length from wide of the crease. De Villiers works this through square leg for a brace. He moves to 46 with this.
On the pads, flicked away towards square leg.
This climbs up from a length around off. Elgar does well to block it with soft hands.
Fuller from round the wicket, flicked away through mid-wicket for a couple.
Bumrah bowls it on a length, de Villiers gets an inside edge to the on side for one.
ABD defends it from within the crease.
This ball is kept out off the front foot.
Another run taken by playing it through point.
That ball has taken the inside edge onto the pads.
FOUR! Nicely played. Shami hurls it on a length outside off, de Villiers camps back and slaps it through cover-point. Huge gap there and hence a boundary is the end result.
Bowled outside off, cut towards point.
Played to the point region by Elgar. They pick up a single.
Outside off, played through point for one.
Shami seems to have missed his run up yet again.
Another ball on off, kept out from the crease.
DE defends it from within the crease.
This one is blocked from the crease.

FOUR! Edged but runs. What are you doing, Parthiv? Clearly the wicketkeeper has to go for such catches. This is a definite chance gone down. Bumrah comes in from round the wicket and bowls a length ball just outside off at 138 kph. The ball zips off the surface and climbs up viciously. Elgar is forced to play at that due to the incoming angle. All he ends up doing is get a thick outside edge. There is a big gap between Patel and Pujara at first slip. The ball flies through there and goes to the fence. Immediately, Patel is seen signaling that it was the first slip's catch and Pujara should have gone for that. Now, this is where Kohli would have loved someone like Saha. He is someone who dives and goes for such acrobatic catches. More than the consequence, it is the effort that matters and Patel has been a let-down in this aspect. What's more, the keeper should have gone for this as it was in the side of his strength, he being a lefty. Elgar lives on as the South African lead swells past 100 now.

Mpumelelo Mbangwa on air tells us that Kohli had an animated chat with the umpire. He says that Virat isn't happy with the visibility there. The commentator reckons that it could be more because India's premier spinner won't be assisted much by these conditions. Another aspect of this arguement could have been that due to a wet outfield, the ball would get wet and that will make it difficult for the bowlers to grip the same.
This is outside off, played through point for a run.
Angled in on a length around off, defended to mid-wicket.
With overcast conditions on offer, Jasprit Bumrah is brought back for a spell. 5-2-19-2 read his current figures.
Fuller on the stumps, flicked away through mid-wicket for one.

Welcome back! The dark clouds haven't gone away completely although the rain has. As a result the floodlights have been switched on. The men concerned are out in the middle and in their respective positions. Shami will run in and de Villiers will face the last ball of the incomplete over...
1615 local time update - Hoila! Rejoice folks! The news coming in from the venue is that play should resume in another 5 minutes. No overs are lost and the it can carry on till 1830.

1520 local time update - Now, now, now! This isn't good news for the cricket lovers. The rain has started to pour down, forcing the players and the umpires off the field. The center is quickly covered. Michael Holding on air says that when the rain stops, resumption shouldn't take time as the drainage facilities are quite good and the outfield might be thirsty as well.
Now Shami has to abort his run up yet again. This time de Villiers isn't happy with something in front of the sightscreen.
Length ball, defended off the back foot with a straight bat.
Sprayed down the leg side, de Villiers misses the flick.
This ball is driven towards mid off.
Another clatter of thunder. This makes the groundsmen alert, who react as school children do after the end-of-day school bell rings.
Fuller on off, driven back down the ground.
Shami misses his run up and aborts bowling this one.
Length ball on off, blocked from the crease.
This one is flicked off the pads towards square leg for nothing.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Elgar defends this towards point.
Owing to the big hit in the previous Ashwin over, mid on has been pushed back now.
A run taken as AB goes back and works it past short leg.
The dark clouds would be a relief to the bowler,  quips Sunil Gavaskar on air.

Floated full outside off, de Villiers looks to sweep it away. Fails to make contact with the ball as his bat hit the ground. A stifled appeal, dies down quickly. Kohli asks Ashwin if the impact was outside off, to which the bowler replies in the affirmative. End of story.
Floated on off, defended off the front foot onto the ground.
This is around off, defended from the crease.

Sound of thunder goes around the ground. This draws huge cheers from the crowd at Centurion. Rain coming in? The forecast didn't show any such signs. A huge dark cloud is hovering above the ground at the moment.
Fuller on off from round the wicket, Elgar keeps it out towards mid on.
AB de Villiers clips this through mid-wicket and gets to the other end.
Outside off, left alone.
This one is defended off the inner half towards mid on.
Length ball on off, defended towards mid off.
Pushed to the cover region by DE.
Flatter on off, defended from the crease.

SIX! Wow! The first biggie in the game comes in the third innings of the Test match. This is floated in line of the stumps, Elgar clears his front leg and hits it over long on for half a dozen. Just clears the ropes though.
This one is bunted off the front foot onto the ground.
Elgar misses flicking it and gets hit high on the pads.
Bowled around off, Elgar stays back and defends it with a straight bat.
As expected, R Ashwin bowl from the other end.
This one is punched to the man at covers.
This is around off, kept out from the crease.
AB gets behind the line of the ball and blocks it down.
Full on off, driven to mid on. Jadeja does the fielding there, not sure for whom he is in.
Length ball outside off, moves in after pitching. De Villiers covers his stumps and lets it go.
Hurled fuller in length around off and middle, defended from the crease with a straight bat.

Here we are. 37 overs to go in the day's play. A fairly long session, like it has been for the past couple of days. We should get most of them as Ashwin will be seen in action for most time. Dean Elgar and AB de Villiers stride out to resume their vigil. Mohammed Shami will start off this session. A wide slip in position.
... Day 3, Session 3 ...

Earlier, the visitors were bowled out 28 short of where the Proteas ended up in their first essay. Kohli was the one man army who made this possible, scoring almost 50 percent of his side's runs. After that, Bumrah came out breathing fire to send Markram and Amla packing. Ashwin went about working with his bag of tricks. Expect more of the tweaker on resumption. See you soon.

Good to see some friendly chat between Kohli and Elgar there. Shows that the fierce competition is limited to the bat-ball contest and not beyond it. South Africa are effectively 88/2 at this point. The tourists would have loved some more wickets after conceding the advantage after the first innings to the opposition. AB de Villiers is in the middle of it all yet again, being unbeaten on 33 in the stand worth 57. Elgar's stay seemed like treading on a minefield but he has come out of it unscathed. The Indians gave nothing away in the time out there so far. They'll look to further this outing come the next session.
Straighter just outside off, Dean just lets it be. That's it from the session. TEA, DAY 3!
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Loopy ball around off, it creates a mini-explosion on the track and spins away. Dean strides forward to defend but the ball just beats the outer edge.
Bunted off the front foot onto the ground.
Indians are right on the money here. Elgar looks to tap it to point and get to the safety of the other end. Ishant Sharma there is alert and doesn't let that happen. Gets the skipper's praise.
Floated on middle and leg, worked away through square leg for one.
With 2 minutes to go, this could be the last over before Tea.
Fuller on off, guided through the point region for one.
Length ball around off, defended towards cover-point.
Straighter and fast at 140 kph on off. ABD stands tall and defends.
Slower off cutter on a fuller length around off and middle. Driven straight to Rohit at mid-wicket who cops a blow to his bread basket owing to the bad bounce that he got.
Similar length ball, de Villiers just gets a half-stride forward and leaves it alone.
Full outside off, left alone.
Blocked from the crease towards point.

Beautiful come back from Ash. Flighted ball around off, spins away after pitching. Elgar is forward in defense but fails to get bat to that. Shouts heard for caught behind but the umpire tells them to carry on.

FOUR! 2nd full toss from Ashwin in the last 6 balls that he has bowled to Elgar. He is letting him off the hook here. This one is a juicy one. The line is on the stumps. Dean gets down and sweeps it through square leg for a boundary.
Slider around off, blocked back towards the bowler.
Floated on off, bunted off the front foot onto the ground.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
This one is worked to the man at mid-wicket.
This is outside off, left alone.
Length ball on the pads, Dean misses the flick and it goes off his thigh pads towards backward square leg. There is a shout heard from someone in the slips. A leg bye taken.

That brings up 50 runs between Elgar and de Villiers. Out of that, the latter has scored 31. Shows his value to the side. He taps this one towards cover-point and sets across to the other end. The hosts seem to be on track for a recovery.
Length ball around off, de Villiers gets an inside edge onto his pads as he looks to defend.

The shape of the ball is looked into. The Indians aren't happy with it and hand it to the umpire. He has a look at it after passing it through the 8-shaped gauge and deem it fit to continue. Wonder why you would change a cherry that has given you two quick wickets.

FOUR! 50 up for South Africa. Once again de Villiers is in the midst of a recovery for them. This is bowled full in line of the stumps, de Villiers push-drives it down the ground. Ashwin starts chasing it. Once that happens, it isn't wrong to assume a boundary resulting. The partnership is worth 49.
On the pads, flicked past short leg for one.
Elgar taps it in front of square leg and crosses over. Kohli not happy with this.
FOUR! This one is the shot that he has played with control against the spinner. Tossed up around middle, Elgar takes it on the full and flicks it through mid-wicket. It goes to the fence in a trice.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Dropped? It will be harsh to use the term but technically it is one. Floated full outside off, Elgar looks to drive it with the spin. Hits it low to Rahul at silly point. The ball hits his fingertips and hits the ground between his legs.
Floated on off, defended off the inner half towards square leg.
Fuller on the stumps, driven towards mid on.
Bumper in line of the stumps, ABD ducks under that.
This one is guided through point for one more.

Streaky runs is what Elgar is accumulating. He moves on to 13 with that, an unlucky number if you'd so believe. This one is delivered fuller in length, he looks to drive it down the ground. Gets a thick outside edge that takes the ball through point. Two runs added to the tally as a result.
Elgar stays in the crease and blocks it out.
Outside off, guided through point for one.
This one is turned past short leg for one.

FOUR! The first real bad ball from Ashwin in this innings. Drops this way short and just outside off. De Villiers isn't someone who will let go of such scoring opportunities. Gets back in a flash and cuts it fiercely through point for a boundary.
Poor from Shami. Elgar gets ahead and drives it straight to covers, where Shami lets it through. That enables the batters to rotate strike.
DE shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Elgar lunges forward and bunts it down with a straight bat.
Flatter on the stumps, punched off the back foot towards covers.
Driven straight to the man at mid on.
This is outside off, left alone.
Fuller on off, blocked from the crease.

FOUR! Timing. That's all about this stroke. This is pitched up fuller at 141 kph. De Villiers gets his front foot forward and just pushed it through mid off for a boundary. Third boundary for him and he moves to 19.
This is outside off at 141 kph, AB shoulders arms to it. Surely, Patel's hands must be feeling the pinch.
Begins with a ball outside off, left alone.
Ishant Sharma to have a bowl now. He was impressive in the first essay, picking a 3-wicket haul.

Are we playing at the MA Chidambaram, asks my colleague KI. You won't be faulted for thinking on the same lines either as the ball is turning square. This one is well flighted, beats the southpaw with the spin away. Ashwin looks to be in rhythm here.
Straighter one this time outside off, AB goes back and guides it past slip for one.
He stays back to this one and blocks this out.

Close! Flatter trajectory, shorter length. Seeing this de Villiers goes back to cut. Ends up getting an inside edge that lobs off his boot. Thankfully for him, it lands it the vacant silly point region.
Blocked off the front foot.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Another appeal for the Indians. Do a Ctrl F to to find out how many times this has happened in this innings. Length ball outside off, Elgar gets his bat down hurriedly to block. Misses and there is an appeal for caught behind. Tuned down. Another good over from Bumrah.
Worked away to the leg side off the pads for one.
Driven towards the mid off region.
On the pads, flicked away through square leg. Pandya chases it down and keeps it down to two.
Beaten! On a length outside off, AB looks to defend that but then withdraws his bat. Is late on doing so as the ball passes the edge of the bat.
FOUR! Shot. Nicely played. On a length outside off, de Villiers stays tall on the back foot and punches it through cover-point. Finds the gap there and gets a boundary.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.

What is Elgar up to here? He isn't looking at ease against Ashwin and yet looks to take him on. Gets down the track and looks to go over the top. Ends up slicing it over mid off. Ishant runs backward but fails to get to it. Two runs taken.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flatter on the pads, Elgar fails to flick it and wears it on the pads. Stifled appeal, turned down.
This one is pushed towards covers.
Floated on the pads, nudged away through square leg for a brave.
This is wide outside off, left alone.
Outside off, left alone.
The batsman gets an inside edge on that which goes fine down the leg side. They pick up a single.

Nice observation. There is a bowlers' map that shows that South Africa have bowled just 5 balls in the line of stumps this morning. Michael Holding on air states about those that aren't on the stumps, that the length is a bit short. That means, those aren't driving length balls. Futile stuff he concludes.
FOUR! Edged but safe. This is angled away from Elgar on a length. He looks to play the drive but gets a thick edge. The ball goes to the third man fence for a boundary.
Nudged fine down the leg side for a single.

Another appeal for caught behind! De Villiers goes for the pull to the short ball but seems to have missed it. The slip cordon yells in appeal though. Another look shows that the ball has indeed missed the bat.

WIDE! Patel leaps high and stops that well. Goalkeeper stuff! Banged short outside off, AB arches back to let it go. It bounces well over the batter's head and the keeper had to jump up full length to collect that.
This one is blocked off the front foot onto the ground.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Lovely ball. Tossed up outside off, draws Dean forward and beats his outside edge.

Another appeal. Indians think that something will happen on every ball. Ashwin bowls this quicker and straighter in line of the stumps, Elgar goes back to flick it but misses. Gets hit high on the thigh pad. Ashwin appeals to no avail.
Outside off, AB reverse sweeps it through backward point for one.
Floated outside off, de Villiers lunges forward and blocks.
Wide outside off, Elgar lets it be.
The batsman gets an inside edge and the ball hits him on the pads. They pick up a single.
FOUR! Excellent delivery to get first up! Bumrah bowls a yorker on middle, de Villiers somehow manages to get his bat down in time as he gets an inside edge, down towards fine leg for a boundary.
AB de Villiers walks out. His team is in trouble here and he needs to bail them out, like he has done on many occasions.

OUT! That is plumb! Bumrah gets his second and he is breathing fire here! Once again it is the ball which comes in that does the trick for him. He steams in and bowls it on a length around off, he gets some inward movement and it also stays low. Amla tries to defend it off the back foot which is probably not a good idea on this wicket. He misses to get hit on the pads. Bumrah, once again, is celebrating even before the umpire raises his finger and Amla straightaway walks off after being given out. A big wicket for the Indians and both the run scorers from the first innings are in the hut now. South Africa are effectively 31 for 2.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
On a length around off, Amla defends it stoutly.
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman.
Tosses it up on middle, driven to mid off.
Tosses it up on off, Elgar drives it to covers.

Another appeal against Elgar but not given! Ashwin bowls a straighter ball on middle, Elgar tries to defend but the ball takes the inside edge onto the pads. Ashwin appeals but the umpire remains put. The Indians are bowling really well here.
Flicks it with the angle towards mid-wicket.
Works it with the spin, towards square leg for a run.
Length outside off, Elgar lets it be.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
A yorker on off, Elgar does well to keep it out.
Good length on off, defended off the front foot.
Good length around off, angling away. Elgar lets it be.

A huge appeal but an inside edge saves him there! Bumrah goes for the yorker but ends up bowling a full toss. Elgar tries to work it through but gets an inside edge onto his pads. The player appeals but the umpire shakes his head.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Gives it air on off, Amla defends it.

Sloppy form India! Elgar drives this full ball towards mid on. He initially thinks about a run but then opts against it. Bumrah there is quick to the ball and fires a wayward throw towards Patel. He jumps and tries to collect but the ball goes above his glove and also beats Kohli who is behind the keeper, trying to catch the ball. It goes down towards fine leg for an overthrow. Needless run given there and Kohli is not a happy man.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Floats it on off, Elgar prods forward and keeps it out.
Tosses it up on off, Elgar lunges forward and keeps it out.
Good length on off, defended solidly.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Almost another one! The ball is staying low here! Bumrah comes running in and lands it on a length around off. it stays a touch low and also jags back in. Amla tries to defend but it takes the inside edge onto his pads.
Length ball outside off, Amla lets it be.
Hashim Amla walks out at no. 3. he showed signs of getting back into form in the last innings. Can he continue it?

OUT! Bumrah strikes! There goes the first one! The ideal start for India. He comes running in and lands it on a length around off, it shapes back in sharply and also stays low. Markram is undone by the low bounce as he hops and tries to defend but misses to get hit on the pads. Bumrah is up and running in celebration as he appeals, he does not even bother looking at the umpire who after a thought raises his finger. Aiden walks down, has a look at the surface and walks off without reviewing. The Indians are ecstatic as they have Markram cheaply this time.
Good length outside off, Markram lets it be.
Jasprit Bumrah to bowl from the other end.
Bowls the carrom ball on off, it spins the other way. Markram tries to defend but it goes off the outside edge, down towards third man for a run.
Once again bowls a flighted ball on off, gets it to turn in, it also bounces a touch more. The ball hits the sticker of Markram's bat as he tries to defend.
The batsman has played it to the point region.
Slower through the air, Markram prods forward in defense.
Gives it air on off, Markram lunges forward and keeps it out.
Tosses it up on off, Markram defends it solidly.
